claims.quote: One particular instance of note of this phenomenon is the "Beast of Exmoor" (sometimes referred to as the "Exmoor Beast").

claims.statement: Sightings were reported as early as 1970, and the story became national news in the United Kingdom in 1983.
claims.statement_id: Penampakannya dilaporkan sejak 1970, dan kisahnya menjadi berita nasional di Britania Raya pada 1983.
claims.quote: with sightings of the creature reported as early as 1970, the story came to national prominence in the United Kingdom in 1983

claims.statement: No big cat has ever been confirmed behind the 1983 livestock killings, which are now attributed to causes such as large dogs.
claims.statement_id: Tidak ada kucing besar yang pernah dipastikan menjadi penyebab pembantaian ternak 1983; kejadian itu kini dikaitkan dengan penyebab lain seperti anjing besar.
claims.quote: no large cat has ever been positively identified to explain such incidents as the 1983 livestock slayings, with them now being attributed to other causes like large dogs.

claims.statement: A national newspaper reported a carcass said to be the Beast of Exmoor that later proved to be a dead seal.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah koran nasional memberitakan bangkai yang diduga Beast of Exmoor, yang kemudian ternyata anjing laut mati.
claims.quote: one national newspaper reported the discovery of a carcass alleged to be the Beast of Exmoor that was later identified as a dead seal.

claims.statement: The Beast of Exmoor is a cryptozoological cat reported to roam rural Exmoor, especially Devon and Somerset, United Kingdom.
claims.statement_id: Beast of Exmoor adalah kucing kriptozoologi yang dilaporkan berkeliaran di pedesaan Exmoor, terutama Devon dan Somerset, Britania Raya.
claims.quote: La bestia di Exmoor è un felino della criptozoologia (vedi gatto fantasma) che è stato segnalato vagare nelle aree rurali di Exmoor, in particolare Devon e Somerset, nel Regno Unito.

claims.statement: It came fully into the spotlight in 1983, when more than a hundred sheep were killed with torn throats at South Molton over three months and blamed on the creature.
claims.statement_id: Ia benar-benar menjadi sorotan pada 1983, ketika lebih dari seratus domba mati dengan leher terkoyak di South Molton dalam tiga bulan dan kematiannya dikaitkan dengan makhluk ini.
claims.quote: fu pienamente al centro dei riflettori solo nel 1983, quando oltre cento pecore furono uccise, con la gola squarciata, a South Molton nell'arco di tre mesi, e la cui uccisione fu attribuita all'essere.

claims.statement: Described with dark grey or black fur, it was thought to be a black leopard or puma released illegally.
claims.statement_id: Bulunya digambarkan abu-abu gelap atau hitam, dan diduga ia macan tutul hitam atau puma yang dilepas secara ilegal.
claims.quote: Descritta col pelo grigio scuro o nero, si è pensato che si potesse trattare di qualche leopardo nero o coguaro liberato illegalmente

claims.statement: In Caribbean folklore the Lusca is a sea monster said to live around the blue holes near Andros, an island in the Bahamas.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Karibia, Lusca adalah monster laut yang konon hidup di kawasan blue hole dekat Andros, sebuah pulau di Bahama.
claims.quote: In Caribbean folklore, the Lusca is a name given to an alleged sea monster said to exist in the region of the blue holes nearby Andros, an island in The Bahamas.

claims.statement: The first report resembling the Lusca came in 1872, when J. S. George of Nassau wrote to the American Naturalist about a "colossal octopus" found dead on the beach.
claims.statement_id: Laporan pertama yang mirip gambaran Lusca muncul pada 1872, ketika J. S. George dari Nassau menulis ke American Naturalist tentang "gurita raksasa" yang ditemukan mati di pantai.
claims.quote: The first reported sighting of something resembling the traditional description of the Lusca in the area was in 1872, when J. S. George of Nassau in the Bahamas wrote to the American Naturalist describing a "colossal octopus" found dead on the beach.

claims.statement: Marine biologist Bruce S. Wright was told by a local guide that limestone caves under a lake were home to the lusca, a large half-octopus, half-dragon animal with sucker-tipped tentacles.
claims.statement_id: Ahli biologi laut Bruce S. Wright mendengar dari pemandu setempat bahwa gua kapur di bawah sebuah danau dihuni lusca, makhluk besar setengah gurita setengah naga dengan tentakel bermangkuk isap.
claims.quote: marine biologist Bruce S. Wright was told by a local guide that some limestone caverns beneath a lake were home to a monster called the lusca, described as a large, half-octopus, half-dragon animal, with powerful, sucker-tipped tentacles, which lived in banana holes and blue holes.

claims.statement: Lusca is a clipped form of Mollusca, referring to the creature's mollusc features such as tentacles.
claims.statement_id: Nama Lusca adalah penggalan dari Mollusca, merujuk pada ciri moluska makhluk ini seperti tentakel.
claims.quote: Lusca is a clipped form of Mollusca (a phylum containing octopus, squid, cuttlefish, and other cephalopods), referring to the creature's varied mollusk features, such as tentacles.

claims.statement: It is described as a giant octopus, a giant cuttlefish, or half shark, half octopus.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan sebagai gurita raksasa, sotong raksasa, atau setengah hiu setengah gurita.
claims.quote: It is described as a giant octopus, a giant cuttlefish, or a half shark, half octopus.

claims.statement: The St. Augustine monster found on the Florida coast in 1896 is considered one of the best candidates for a lusca specimen.
claims.statement_id: Monster St. Augustine yang terdampar di pantai Florida pada 1896 dianggap salah satu kandidat terkuat spesimen lusca.
claims.quote: Le monstre de St. Augustin qui a été trouvé sur les côtes de Floride en 1896 est l'un des meilleurs candidats pour un possible spécimen de lusca.

claims.statement: The Minhocão is a creature of Brazilian folklore variously said to be a large fish or worm-like.
claims.statement_id: Minhocão adalah makhluk cerita rakyat Brasil yang diklaim berupa ikan besar atau menyerupai cacing.
claims.quote: is a creature from Brazilian folklore that is variously claimed to be a large fish or resembling a worm

claims.statement: Locals in Brazil described the Minhocão to European explorers and naturalists in the 19th century.
claims.statement_id: Penduduk Brasil menceritakan Minhocão kepada penjelajah dan naturalis Eropa pada abad ke-19.
claims.quote: The Minhocão was described to European explorers and naturalists in the 19th century by locals in Brazil.

claims.statement: French naturalist Augustin Saint-Hilaire recorded in December 1846 accounts of Minhocão in the Padre Aranda and Feia lakes that often dragged horses and cattle under water.
claims.statement_id: Naturalis Prancis Augustin Saint-Hilaire pada Desember 1846 mencatat kisah Minhocão di danau Padre Aranda dan Feia yang konon sering menyeret kuda dan sapi ke dalam air.
claims.quote: French naturalist Augustin Saint-Hilaire described in December 1846 accounts of the Minhocão in the Padre Aranda and Feia lakes, with claims that they lived in the lakes and had "often drawn horses and horned cattle under the water".

claims.statement: He concluded that Minhocão is an augmentative of minhoca, Portuguese for earthworm.
claims.statement_id: Ia menyimpulkan Minhocão adalah bentuk pembesar dari minhoca, kata Portugis untuk cacing tanah.
claims.quote: He determined 'Minhocão' to be an augmentative of 'minhoca', Portuguese for earthworm.

claims.statement: Saint-Hilaire guessed it might be a large species of South American lungfish.
claims.statement_id: Saint-Hilaire menduga Minhocão itu sejenis ikan paru Amerika Selatan yang besar.
claims.quote: Saint-Hilaire speculated that the Minhocão described to him may be a large species of South American lungfish.

claims.statement: It was also reported by German naturalist Fritz Müller in a German scientific journal in 1878.
claims.statement_id: Minhocão juga dilaporkan naturalis Jerman Fritz Müller dalam jurnal ilmiah Jerman pada 1878.
claims.quote: It was also reported in an article in a German scientific journal in 1878 by German naturalist Dr. Fritz Müller

claims.statement: It was said to uproot trees, leave deep trenches in its path and prefer damp conditions.
claims.statement_id: Ia konon mencabut pohon, meninggalkan parit dalam di jalurnya, dan menyukai tempat lembap.
claims.quote: It was said to uproot trees and leave deep trenches in its path, and to prefer damp conditions.

claims.statement: Cryptozoologist Karl Shuker suggested a link with the Sachamama, a cryptid of Peru.
claims.statement_id: Kriptozoolog Karl Shuker menduga ada kaitan dengan Sachamama, kriptid dari Peru.
claims.quote: 未確認生物学者のカール・シューカーは、ペルーに出現するサチャママ（Sachamama）という未確認動物との関連を示唆した。

claims.statement: The Patagons or Patagonian giants were a mythical race of giant humans said in early European accounts to live in Patagonia.
claims.statement_id: Patagon atau raksasa Patagonia adalah ras manusia raksasa mitos yang konon tinggal di Patagonia menurut catatan Eropa awal.
claims.quote: The Patagons or Patagonian giants were a mythical race of giant humans rumoured to be living in Patagonia described in early European accounts.

claims.statement: They were said to be at least twice normal human height, some accounts giving 13 to 15 feet.
claims.statement_id: Mereka disebut setidaknya dua kali tinggi manusia biasa, dengan beberapa catatan menyebut 13 hingga 15 kaki.
claims.quote: They were said to have exceeded at least double normal human height, with some accounts giving heights of 13 to 15 feet

claims.statement: Tales of them shaped European ideas of the region for nearly 300 years.
claims.statement_id: Kisah mereka memengaruhi gambaran Eropa tentang wilayah itu selama hampir 300 tahun.
claims.quote: Tales of these people maintained a hold upon European conceptions of the region for nearly 300 years.

claims.statement: The first mention came from Ferdinand Magellan and his crew, who claimed to see them while sailing the South American coast during their 1520s circumnavigation.
claims.statement_id: Penyebutan pertama berasal dari pelayaran Ferdinand Magellan dan awaknya, yang mengaku melihat mereka saat menyusuri pantai Amerika Selatan dalam pelayaran keliling dunia tahun 1520-an.
claims.quote: The first mention of these people came from the voyage of Ferdinand Magellan and his crew, who claimed to have seen them while exploring the coastline of South America en route to the Maluku Islands in their circumnavigation of the world in the 1520s.

claims.statement: The voyage account says a naked man of giant stature was seen on the shore, dancing, singing and throwing dust on his head.
claims.statement_id: Catatan pelayaran itu menyebut seorang lelaki telanjang bertubuh raksasa terlihat di pantai, menari, bernyanyi, dan menaburkan debu di kepalanya.
claims.quote: One day we suddenly saw a naked man of giant stature on the shore of the port, dancing, singing, and throwing dust on his head.

claims.statement: He was so tall that the sailors reached only to his waist.
claims.statement_id: Ia begitu tinggi sehingga para pelaut hanya setinggi pinggangnya.
claims.quote: He was so tall that we reached only to his waist, and he was well proportioned

claims.statement: Pigafetta recorded that Magellan gave these people the name Patagão.
claims.statement_id: Pigafetta mencatat bahwa Magellan memberi mereka nama Patagão.
claims.quote: Pigafetta also recorded that Magellan had bestowed on these people the name "Patagão"

claims.statement: The Patagon story was believed for 250 years until it was disproved in the late 18th century.
claims.statement_id: Cerita tentang Patagon dipercaya selama 250 tahun hingga dibuktikan tidak benar pada akhir abad ke-18.
claims.quote: Cerita mengenai Patagon ini terus dipercaya selama 250 tahun, hingga dibuktikan kebohongannya pada akhir abad ke-18.

claims.statement: The place name Patagonia comes from the meaning "land where the Patagons live".
claims.statement_id: Nama wilayah Patagonia berasal dari arti "tanah tempat tinggal Patagon".
claims.quote: 現在の南米パタゴニアの地名は「パタゴンの住む土地」の意からきている。

claims.statement: The Pope Lick Monster is a legendary part-man, part-goat, part-sheep creature said to live under a railroad trestle over Pope Lick Creek in Louisville, Kentucky.
claims.statement_id: Pope Lick Monster adalah makhluk legendaris setengah manusia, setengah kambing dan domba yang konon hidup di bawah jembatan kereta di atas Pope Lick Creek, Louisville, Kentucky.
claims.quote: is a legendary part-man, part-goat and part-sheep creature reported to live beneath a railroad trestle bridge over Pope Lick Creek, in the Fisherville neighborhood of Louisville, Kentucky, United States.

claims.statement: Some accounts say it uses hypnosis or voice mimicry to lure trespassers onto the trestle to die before an oncoming train.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sebagian kisah, ia memakai hipnosis atau peniruan suara untuk memikat orang ke jembatan hingga tewas tertabrak kereta.
claims.quote: According to some accounts, the creature uses either hypnosis or voice mimicry to lure trespassers onto the trestle to meet their death before an oncoming train.

claims.statement: Other stories say it jumps from the trestle onto the roofs of passing cars.
claims.statement_id: Kisah lain menyebut ia melompat dari jembatan ke atap mobil yang lewat di bawahnya.
claims.quote: Other stories claim the monster jumps down from the trestle onto the roofs of cars passing beneath it.

claims.statement: Other legends say it was a circus performer who vowed revenge after being mistreated.
claims.statement_id: Legenda lain menyebut ia dulunya penampil sirkus yang bersumpah membalas dendam setelah dianiaya.
claims.quote: Other legends hold that the monster is a human-goat hybrid, and that it was a circus freak who vowed revenge after being mistreated.

claims.statement: The legends made the area a legend-tripping site, and there have been several deaths and accidents at the trestle since it was built.
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini menjadikan tempat itu tujuan wisata legenda, dan sejak jembatan dibangun sudah terjadi sejumlah kematian dan kecelakaan di sana.
claims.quote: The legends have turned the area into a site for legend tripping. There have been a number of deaths and accidents at the trestle since its construction

claims.statement: In reality the bridge carries a major rail line into Louisville.
claims.statement_id: Kenyataannya, jembatan itu masih dilalui jalur kereta utama menuju Louisville.
claims.quote: in reality, the bridge carries a major rail artery into Louisville.

claims.statement: It is often nicknamed Goat Man or sometimes Sheepman.
claims.statement_id: Ia sering dijuluki Goat Man (manusia kambing) atau kadang Sheepman (manusia domba).
claims.quote: souvent surnommé Goat Man, « l'homme-bouc » ou parfois Sheepman, « l'homme-mouton »

claims.statement: The Sihuanaba is a supernatural entity of Central American folklore with regional variants in parts of Mexico.
claims.statement_id: Sihuanaba adalah makhluk gaib dari cerita rakyat Amerika Tengah, dengan varian di sebagian Meksiko.
claims.quote: The Sihuanaba is a supernatural entity originating in Central American folklore, with related regional variants present across parts of Mexico.

claims.statement: It is a shapeshifting spirit that appears as an attractive long-haired woman to deceive people from afar.
claims.statement_id: Ia roh pengubah wujud yang tampil sebagai perempuan menarik berambut panjang untuk menipu orang dari kejauhan.
claims.quote: the entity functions as a shapeshifting spirit that adopts the appearance of an attractive, long haired woman to deceive observers from a distance.

claims.statement: It lures lone men to isolated or dangerous places before revealing its true form, a fleshless skull or a horse's head.
claims.statement_id: Ia memikat pria yang sendirian ke tempat terpencil atau berbahaya, lalu menampakkan wujud aslinya: tengkorak tanpa daging atau kepala kuda.
claims.quote: it entices solitary men into isolated or hazardous environments prior to revealing a grotesque true form, commonly represented as a fleshless skull or the head of a horse.

claims.statement: Scholars suggest the Sihuanaba and its variants came from Spain and reached Latin America in the colonial period.
claims.statement_id: Para ahli menduga Sihuanaba dan variannya berasal dari Spanyol dan dibawa ke Amerika Latin pada masa kolonial.
claims.quote: Scholars hypothesize that the Sihuanaba and its variants originated in Spain and were introduced to Latin America during the colonial period.

claims.statement: Spanish colonists used the legend as a tool of social control over Indigenous and mestizo people.
claims.statement_id: Penjajah Spanyol memakai legenda ini sebagai alat kendali sosial atas penduduk pribumi dan mestizo.
claims.quote: Spanish colonists adapted the legend as an instrument of social control over Indigenous and mestizo populations.

claims.statement: She is often met washing clothes or bathing in rivers and other waters.
claims.statement_id: Ia sering dijumpai sedang mencuci pakaian atau mandi di sungai dan perairan lain.
claims.quote: She is commonly encountered washing clothing or bathing in rivers, streams, and other bodies of water.

claims.statement: The sudden sight of her face is said to make victims die of fright or go mad.
claims.statement_id: Wajah aslinya yang tiba-tiba terlihat konon membuat korban mati ketakutan atau menjadi gila.
claims.quote: This sudden revelation is said to induce severe shock, causing victims to either die of fright or descend into madness.

claims.statement: The Sihuanaba is also called Siguanaba, Cigua or Cegua.
claims.statement_id: Sihuanaba juga disebut Siguanaba, Cigua, atau Cegua.
claims.quote: La Sihuanaba, La Siguanaba, Cigua ou Cegua est un personnage surnaturel du folklore d'Amérique centrale.

claims.statement: A soucouyant is a kind of shape-shifting, blood-sucking hag of Caribbean folklore.
claims.statement_id: Soucouyant adalah sejenis nenek sihir pengubah wujud dan pengisap darah dalam cerita rakyat Karibia.
claims.quote: is a kind of shape-shifting, blood-sucking hag present in Caribbean folklore.

claims.statement: In Guyana, Belize and Jamaica it is called Ol' Higue or Ole Haig.
claims.statement_id: Di Guyana, Belize, dan Jamaika ia disebut Ol' Higue atau Ole Haig.
claims.quote: Ol' Higue or Ole Haig in Guyana, Belize and Jamaica

claims.statement: By day the Soucouyant looks like a reclusive old woman (or man); at night it strips off its wrinkled skin, puts it in a mortar and flies as a fireball in search of a victim.
claims.statement_id: Pada siang hari Soucouyant tampak sebagai perempuan (atau lelaki) tua penyendiri; pada malam hari ia melepas kulit keriputnya, menaruhnya di lesung, lalu terbang sebagai bola api mencari korban.
claims.quote: The Soucouyant is a folklore character who appears as a reclusive old woman (or man) by day. By night, they strip off their wrinkled skin and put it in a mortar. In the form of a fireball, they fly across the dark sky in search of a victim.

claims.statement: Soucouyants suck blood from the arms, necks and legs of sleeping victims, leaving black and blue marks by morning.
claims.statement_id: Soucouyant mengisap darah dari lengan, leher, dan kaki korban yang tidur, meninggalkan memar biru kehitaman pada pagi harinya.
claims.quote: Soucouyants suck humans' blood from their arms, necks, legs and other soft regions while the victim sleeps, leaving black and blue marks on the body in the morning.

claims.statement: They trade their victims' blood for evil powers with Bazil, the demon living in the silk cotton tree.
claims.statement_id: Mereka menukar darah korban dengan kekuatan jahat dari Bazil, iblis yang tinggal di pohon kapuk.
claims.quote: Soucouyants trade their victims' blood for evil powers with Bazil, the demon who resides in the silk cotton tree.

claims.statement: To expose a soucouyant, people heap rice around the house or at the village crossroads; it must gather the rice grain by grain and is caught in the act.
claims.statement_id: Untuk membongkar soucouyant, orang menaburkan beras di sekitar rumah atau di persimpangan desa; makhluk itu terpaksa memungutinya butir demi butir hingga tertangkap basah.
claims.quote: To expose a soucouyant, it is believed one should heap rice around their house or at the village crossroads; the creature will be obligated to gather the rice, grain by grain, and be caught in the act.

claims.statement: In Trinidad and Tobago the soucouyant is a mythological blood-sucking being.
claims.statement_id: Di Trinidad dan Tobago, soucouyant adalah makhluk mitologis pengisap darah.
claims.quote: Eine Soucouyant ist in Trinidad und Tobago ein mythologisches, blutsaugendes Wesen.

claims.statement: A Christian cross in the window is believed to protect a house from the soucouyant.
claims.statement_id: Salib Kristen di jendela rumah dipercaya melindungi dari pengaruh soucouyant.
claims.quote: Steht am Fenster des Hauses ein christliches Kreuz, so soll dies vor dem Einfluss der Soucouyant schützen.

claims.statement: The squonk is a mythical creature said to live in the hemlock forests of northern Pennsylvania, United States.
claims.statement_id: Squonk adalah makhluk mitos yang konon hidup di hutan hemlock Pennsylvania utara, Amerika Serikat.
claims.quote: The squonk is a mythical creature that is reputed to live in the hemlock forests of northern Pennsylvania in the United States.

claims.statement: The first written account of the squonk is in the 1910 book Fearsome Creatures of the Lumberwoods.
claims.statement_id: Catatan tertulis pertama tentang squonk ada dalam buku Fearsome Creatures of the Lumberwoods (1910).
claims.quote: The first written account of the squonk was from the 1910 book Fearsome Creatures of the Lumberwoods.

claims.statement: The 1939 book Fearsome Critters said squonks migrated from deserts to swamps before settling in Pennsylvania.
claims.statement_id: Buku Fearsome Critters (1939) menyebut squonk bermigrasi dari gurun ke rawa lalu menetap di Pennsylvania.
claims.quote: Its provenance was described in the next written iteration, in the 1939 book Fearsome Critters. This book suggested that the creatures had migrated from deserts to swamps to finally settle in Pennsylvania.

claims.statement: Its ill-fitting skin, covered in warts and moles, makes it always unhappy.
claims.statement_id: Kulitnya yang kebesaran dan penuh kutil serta tahi lalat membuatnya selalu sedih.
claims.quote: Because of its misfitting skin, which is covered with warts and moles, it is always unhappy

claims.statement: Hunters can track it by its trail of tears, since it weeps constantly; cornered or frightened, it may even dissolve into tears.
claims.statement_id: Pemburu bisa melacaknya dari jejak air mata karena ia terus menangis; bila terpojok atau ketakutan, ia bahkan bisa larut menjadi air mata.
claims.quote: Hunters who are good at tracking are able to follow a squonk by its tear-stained trail, for the animal weeps constantly. When cornered and escape seems impossible, or when surprised and frightened, it may even dissolve itself in tears.

claims.statement: Johnstown, Pennsylvania, celebrates the squonk at the Squonkapalooza in August.
claims.statement_id: Kota Johnstown, Pennsylvania, merayakan squonk dalam festival Squonkapalooza setiap Agustus.
claims.quote: Johnstown, Pennsylvania celebrates the Squonk at the Squonkapalooza in August.

claims.statement: The squonk is given the "scientific name" Lacrimacorpus dissolvens, Latin words for "tear", "body" and "dissolve".
claims.statement_id: Squonk diberi "nama ilmiah" Lacrimacorpus dissolvens, rangkaian kata Latin untuk "air mata", "tubuh", dan "larut".
claims.quote: スクォンクにはLacrimacorpus dissolvensという「学名」がつけられている。これはラテン語で「涙」「体」「溶ける」の意味の語を羅列したものである。

claims.statement: In the Chilote mythology of Chiloé, Chile, the Trauco is a small, dwarf-like humanoid living deep in the forest, with an ugly face and legs without feet.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Chilote di Chiloé, Chili, Trauco adalah makhluk mirip manusia bertubuh kecil seperti kurcaci yang tinggal jauh di dalam hutan; wajahnya buruk dan kakinya tanpa telapak.
claims.quote: In the traditional Chilote mythology of Chiloé, Chile, the Trauco is a humanoid creature of small stature—similar to a dwarf or goblin—who lives deep in the forest. It has an ugly face and legs without feet.

claims.statement: It is a child of the snake god Coi Coi-Vilu.
claims.statement_id: Ia anak dewa ular Coi Coi-Vilu.
claims.quote: It is a child of the snake god Coi Coi-Vilu.

claims.statement: It has a strong pull on young and middle-aged women; in myth its wife is the wicked, ugly Fiura.
claims.statement_id: Ia punya daya pikat kuat terhadap perempuan muda dan paruh baya; menurut mitos, istrinya adalah Fiura yang jahat dan buruk rupa.
claims.quote: It has a powerful magnetism that attracts young and middle-aged women. According to myth, the Trauco's wife is the wicked and ugly Fiura.

claims.statement: The Trauco carries a small stone-headed hatchet to strike trees in the forest.
claims.statement_id: Trauco membawa kapak kecil berkepala batu untuk memukul pohon di hutan.
claims.quote: The Trauco carries a small stone-headed hatchet that he uses to strike trees in the forest

claims.statement: Some men of Chiloé fear the Trauco, believing his gaze can kill.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian lelaki Chiloé takut pada Trauco karena percaya tatapannya dapat mematikan.
claims.quote: Some men of Chiloé fear the Trauco, as they believe his gaze can be deadly.

claims.statement: When an unmarried woman is pregnant and no man claims fatherhood, people assume Trauco is the father, and she is held blameless because he is irresistible.
claims.statement_id: Bila perempuan lajang hamil tanpa ada lelaki yang mengaku ayahnya, orang menganggap Trauco ayahnya, dan perempuan itu dianggap tidak bersalah karena daya pikatnya tak tertahankan.
claims.quote: When a single woman is pregnant and no one steps forward as the father, people assume that Trauco is the father. Because the creature is irresistible, the woman is considered blameless.

claims.statement: The Trauco looks like an ugly, ogre-faced man no taller than 80 cm, with stumps instead of feet.
claims.statement_id: Trauco berwujud lelaki berwajah buruk seperti raksasa jahat, tingginya tidak lebih dari 80 cm, dan kakinya berupa tunggul tanpa telapak.
claims.quote: El Trauco es un ser con el aspecto de un hombre de facciones desagradables como un ogro, de baja estatura, no midiendo más de 80 cm, y sus piernas tienen muñones y no pies.

claims.statement: He carries a twisted staff called a pahueldún and a small magic stone hatchet.
claims.statement_id: Ia membawa tongkat bengkok bernama pahueldún dan kapak batu kecil yang ajaib.
claims.quote: llevando un bastón retorcido llamado pahueldún y una pequeña y mágica hacha de piedra

claims.statement: Xiuhcōātl was a mythological serpent, the spirit form of the Aztec fire god Xiuhtecuhtli, sometimes shown as an atlatl or weapon of Huitzilopochtli.
claims.statement_id: Xiuhcōātl adalah ular mitologis, wujud roh Xiuhtecuhtli, dewa api Aztek, yang kadang digambarkan sebagai atlatl atau senjata Huitzilopochtli.
claims.quote: was a mythological serpent, regarded as the spirit form of Xiuhtecuhtli, the Aztec fire deity sometimes represented as an atlatl or a weapon wielded by Huitzilopochtli.

claims.statement: Xiuhcoatl is a Classical Nahuatl word meaning "turquoise serpent", and symbolically "fire serpent".
claims.statement_id: Xiuhcoatl adalah kata Nahuatl Klasik yang berarti "ular pirus" dan secara simbolis "ular api".
claims.quote: Xiuhcoatl is a Classical Nahuatl word that translates as "turquoise serpent" and also carries the symbolic and descriptive translation of "fire serpent".

claims.statement: Xiuhcoatl was a common subject of Aztec art, including codices, and appears as a back ornament on images of Xiuhtecuhtli and Huitzilopochtli.
claims.statement_id: Xiuhcoatl sering muncul dalam seni Aztek, termasuk kodeks, dan dipakai sebagai hiasan punggung pada gambar Xiuhtecuhtli dan Huitzilopochtli.
claims.quote: Xiuhcoatl was a common subject of Aztec art, including illustrations in Aztec codices, and was used as a back ornament on representations of both Xiuhtecuhtli and Huitzilopochtli.

claims.statement: Xiuhcoatl is interpreted as the embodiment of the dry season and was the weapon of the sun.
claims.statement_id: Xiuhcoatl ditafsirkan sebagai perwujudan musim kemarau dan merupakan senjata matahari.
claims.quote: Xiuhcoatl is interpreted as the embodiment of the dry season and was the weapon of the sun.

claims.statement: The royal diadem (xiuhuitzolli) of the Aztec emperors apparently represented the tail of Xiuhcoatl.
claims.statement_id: Mahkota kerajaan kaisar Aztek (xiuhuitzolli) tampaknya melambangkan ekor Xiuhcoatl.
claims.quote: Apparently, the royal diadem (or xiuhuitzolli, "pointed turquoise thing") of the Aztec emperors represented the tail of the Xiuhcoatl, the fire serpent.

claims.statement: Xiuhcoatl was usually shown with a sharply back-turned snout and a segmented body.
claims.statement_id: Xiuhcoatl biasanya digambarkan dengan moncong yang melengkung tajam ke belakang dan tubuh beruas-ruas.
claims.quote: Typically, Xiuhcoatl was depicted with a sharply back-turned snout and a segmented body.

claims.statement: Its body was wrapped in knotted paper strips, linking it to bloodletting and sacrifice.
claims.statement_id: Tubuhnya dililit pita kertas bersimpul, yang mengaitkannya dengan ritual penumpahan darah dan persembahan.
claims.quote: The body of the Xiuhcoatl was wrapped with knotted strips of paper, linking the serpent to bloodletting and sacrifice.

claims.statement: In Aztec mythology Xiuhcoatl personifies the dry season and scorched earth.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Aztek, Xiuhcoatl adalah personifikasi musim kemarau dan tanah hangus.
claims.quote: Pada mitologi Aztek, Xiuhcoatl (ular api) adalah personifikasi dari musim kemarau dan tanah hangus.

claims.statement: In his birth story Huitzilopochtli was born armed from Coatlicue and fought with a shield, darts and Xiuhcoatl.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah kelahirannya, Huitzilopochtli lahir dari Coatlicue dalam keadaan bersenjata dan bertempur dengan perisai, tombak lempar, dan Xiuhcoatl.
claims.quote: その時ウィツィロポチトリが武装した姿でコアトリクエから誕生し、盾・投げ矢・シウコアトルで戦った。

claims.statement: The Adlet (or Erqigdlet) are a race of creatures in the Inuit mythology of Greenland and the Labrador and Hudson Bay coasts.
claims.statement_id: Adlet (atau Erqigdlet) adalah ras makhluk dalam mitologi Inuit di Greenland serta pesisir Labrador dan Teluk Hudson.
claims.quote: The Adlet (or Erqigdlet) are a race of creatures in the Inuit mythology of Greenland, as well as the Labrador and Hudson Bay coasts.

claims.statement: The Adlet's lower body is like a dog's and the upper like a man's; they run fast, but encounters with men usually end in the men's favour.
claims.statement_id: Tubuh bagian bawah Adlet seperti anjing dan bagian atasnya seperti manusia; mereka berlari cepat, tetapi pertemuan dengan manusia biasanya dimenangkan manusia.
claims.quote: The lower part of the body of the canine Adlet is like that of a dog and their upper part is like a man's. All Adlet run quickly, and their encounters with men usually end with man as the victor.

claims.statement: In Inuit lore they often clash with humans, are taller than Inuit and white people, and in some stories eat people.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita Inuit mereka sering bermusuhan dengan manusia, lebih tinggi dari orang Inuit dan kulit putih, dan dalam beberapa kisah memakan manusia.
claims.quote: In Inuit lore, they are often portrayed as in conflict with humans, and are supposed to be taller than Inuit and white people. In some stories they are cannibals.

claims.statement: The Labrador and Hudson Bay peoples identified the race descended from the Adlet with inland Native Americans.
claims.statement_id: Suku-suku Labrador dan Teluk Hudson menyamakan ras keturunan Adlet dengan penduduk asli Amerika di pedalaman.
claims.quote: The monstrous race begotten by the Adlet was identified with inland Native Americans by the Labrador and Hudson Bay tribes

claims.statement: H. Newell Wardle proposed that adlet may come from ad, "below", meaning "those below".
claims.statement_id: H. Newell Wardle mengusulkan bahwa adlet mungkin berasal dari ad, "di bawah", sehingga berarti "mereka yang di bawah".
claims.quote: An etymology of the word is proposed by H. Newell Wardle: adlet might come from ad, "below," and thus denote "those below."

claims.statement: In myth the Adlet were born when a beautiful Inuit woman on the shores of Hudson Bay married a giant red dog with supernatural powers.
claims.statement_id: Menurut mitos, Adlet lahir ketika seorang perempuan Inuit yang cantik di tepi Teluk Hudson menikahi anjing merah raksasa berkekuatan gaib.
claims.quote: l'adlet est né lorsqu'une magnifique femme inuite, vivant sur les rives de la baie d'Hudson, a épousé un gigantesque chien rouge doté de pouvoirs surnaturels.

claims.statement: She bore ten children: five puppies like their father and five fierce hybrids with the worst traits of both parents.
claims.statement_id: Ia melahirkan sepuluh anak: lima anak anjing yang mirip ayahnya dan lima makhluk campuran ganas yang mewarisi sifat terburuk kedua orang tuanya.
claims.quote: Neuf mois plus tard, elle donna naissance à dix enfants. Les cinq premiers étaient de petits chiots magnifiques ressemblant à leur père. Cependant, les cinq autres étaient des hybrides féroces étant une combinaison des pires traits des deux parents.

claims.statement: In one version, five of the ten children were wolves who crossed the sea and became the ancestors of the European peoples.
claims.statement_id: Menurut satu versi, lima dari sepuluh anak itu adalah serigala yang menyeberangi laut dan menjadi leluhur bangsa-bangsa Eropa.
claims.quote: Пятеро из десяти детей женщины были волками, которые, согласно мифу, пересекли море и дали начало европейским народам.

claims.statement: In Inuit folklore the akhlut is an orca-like composite animal that becomes a wolf on land, sometimes shown as a wolf-orca hybrid.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Inuit, akhlut adalah hewan gabungan mirip orca yang berwujud serigala di darat, kadang digambarkan sebagai campuran serigala dan orca.
claims.quote: is an orca-like composite animal that takes the form of a wolf when on land, and is sometimes depicted as a wolf-orca hybrid.

claims.statement: In 1900 American naturalist Edward William Nelson described the creature.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1900 naturalis Amerika Edward William Nelson menggambarkan makhluk ini.
claims.quote: In 1900, the American naturalist Edward William Nelson described the

claims.statement: It resembles the killer whale and can turn into a wolf at will; after roaming the land it may return to the sea and become a whale again.
claims.statement_id: Wujudnya mirip paus pembunuh dan ia dapat berubah menjadi serigala sesukanya; setelah berkeliaran di darat ia bisa kembali ke laut dan menjadi paus lagi.
claims.quote: It is described as being similar in form to the killer whale and is credited with the power of changing at will to a wolf; after roaming about over the land it may return to the sea and again become a whale.

claims.statement: These animals are said to be very fierce and to kill men.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini dikatakan sangat ganas dan membunuh manusia.
claims.quote: These animals are said to be very fierce and to kill men.

claims.statement: Nelson explained wolf tracks that seemed to lead into the sea as the result of ice breaking off at the edge.
claims.statement_id: Nelson menjelaskan jejak serigala yang tampak menuju laut sebagai akibat es yang patah di tepinya.
claims.quote: and explained wolf tracks appearing to lead into the sea as the result of ice breaking away from the edge.

claims.statement: The akhlut is a dangerous beast that comes onto land to hunt humans and other animals.
claims.statement_id: Akhlut binatang berbahaya yang naik ke darat untuk memburu manusia dan hewan lain.
claims.quote: Si tratta di una bestia pericolosa che si avventura sulla terra per cacciare gli esseri umani e gli altri animali

claims.statement: The Apotamkin is a creature of Maliseet and Passamaquoddy mythology: a giant fanged sea monster of Passamaquoddy Bay, at the mouth of the St. Croix River, that drags people in to eat them, especially careless children.
claims.statement_id: Apotamkin adalah makhluk dalam mitologi Maliseet dan Passamaquoddy: monster laut raksasa bertaring di Teluk Passamaquoddy, di muara Sungai St. Croix, yang menyeret orang untuk dimakan, terutama anak-anak yang lengah.
claims.quote: is a creature in Maliseet and Passamaquoddy mythology. It is described a giant fanged sea monster that lives in the Passamaquoddy Bay, specifically at the mouth of St. Croix River, and pulls people in to eat them, particularly careless children.

claims.statement: It is sometimes humanoid, sometimes fish-bodied with human hair; its hair is always long and red, and in some versions it was a woman turned into a serpent.
claims.statement_id: Kadang ia digambarkan mirip manusia, kadang bertubuh ikan dengan rambut manusia; rambutnya selalu disebut panjang dan merah, dan dalam beberapa versi ia dulu perempuan yang diubah menjadi ular.
claims.quote: The Apotamkin is sometimes described as being humanoid, and sometimes as having a fully fish body with human hair. It is consistently said to have long red hair, and in some versions, it was a human woman before being changed into a serpent.

claims.statement: In 1888 the Journal of American Folklore described it as mermaid-like.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1888 Journal of American Folklore menggambarkannya mirip putri duyung.
claims.quote: In 1888, the Journal of American Folklore described it as similar to a mermaid.

claims.statement: Its presence keeps children from entering the water unsupervised; the Passamaquoddy believe the Apotamkin keeps children from falling through thin ice.
claims.statement_id: Keberadaannya mencegah anak masuk ke air tanpa pengawasan; orang Passamaquoddy percaya Apotamkin mencegah anak terperosok ke es tipis.
claims.quote: Its presence deters children from entering the water without parental supervision, avoiding injuries or death. The Passamaquoddy tribe believe that the Apotamkin prevents children from falling through thin ice.

claims.statement: Pacific Northwest legends also have an Apotamkin, a tall, ape-like version with orange-brown hair.
claims.statement_id: Legenda Pasifik Barat Laut juga mengenal Apotamkin, tetapi berwujud tinggi seperti kera dengan bulu cokelat jingga.
claims.quote: Legends from the Pacific Northwest also have a monster called an Apotamkin. This version is tall and apelike as opposed to aquatic, with orange-brown hair and fur.

claims.statement: Both versions served as bogeymen to keep children from going into dangerous places alone.
claims.statement_id: Kedua versi dipakai sebagai momok untuk menakut-nakuti anak agar tidak pergi sendirian ke tempat berbahaya.
claims.quote: Both the Northeast and Northwest versions of the Apotamkin were bogyman figures used to instill fear into children to keep them from venturing dangerous areas alone.

claims.statement: The Pacific Northwest version appears in Stephenie Meyer's Twilight.
claims.statement_id: Versi Pasifik Barat Laut muncul dalam Twilight karya Stephenie Meyer.
claims.quote: The Pacific Northwest version of the Apotamkin appears in Stephenie Meyer's Twilight

claims.statement: The Apotamkin is sometimes considered a Native American version of a vampire.
claims.statement_id: Apotamkin kadang dianggap versi vampir dari penduduk asli Amerika.
claims.quote: O Apotamkin às vezes é considerado uma versão nativa americana de um vampiro.

claims.statement: Cocijo is a lightning god of the pre-Columbian Zapotec civilization of southern Mexico.
claims.statement_id: Cocijo adalah dewa petir peradaban Zapotek pra-Kolumbus di Meksiko selatan.
claims.quote: is a lightning deity of the pre-Columbian Zapotec civilization of southern Mexico.

claims.statement: He shares traits with other Mesoamerican rain, thunder and lightning gods, such as Tlaloc of central Mexico and Chaac of the Maya.
claims.statement_id: Ia memiliki ciri dewa hujan, guntur, dan petir Mesoamerika lainnya, seperti Tlaloc dari Meksiko tengah dan Chaac dari peradaban Maya.
claims.quote: He has attributes characteristic of similar Mesoamerican deities associated with rain, thunder and lightning, such as Tlaloc of central Mexico, and Chaac (or Chaak) of the Maya civilization.

claims.statement: In Zapotec, the word cocijo means "lightning" and also names the god.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Zapotek, kata cocijo berarti "petir" sekaligus nama dewanya.
claims.quote: In the Zapotec language, the word cocijo means "lightning", as well as referring to the deity.

claims.statement: Cocijo was the most important god of the pre-Columbian Zapotecs because of his link with rain.
claims.statement_id: Cocijo dewa terpenting bagi orang Zapotek pra-Kolumbus karena kaitannya dengan hujan.
claims.quote: Cocijo was the most important deity among the pre-Columbian Zapotecs because of his association with rainfall.

claims.statement: In Zapotec myth he made the sun, moon, stars, seasons, land, mountains, rivers, plants, animals, and day and night from his breath.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitos Zapotek, ia menciptakan matahari, bulan, bintang, musim, daratan, gunung, sungai, tumbuhan, hewan, serta siang dan malam dari embusan napasnya.
claims.quote: In Zapotec myth, he made the sun, moon, stars, seasons, land, mountains, rivers, plants and animals, and day and night by exhaling and creating everything from his breath.

claims.statement: In Zapotec art Cocijo has an animal-like face with a wide, blunt snout and a long forked serpent tongue.
claims.statement_id: Dalam seni Zapotek, Cocijo digambarkan berwajah hewan dengan moncong lebar tumpul dan lidah ular bercabang yang panjang.
claims.quote: In Zapotec art Cocijo is represented with a zoomorphic face with a wide, blunt snout and a long forked serpentine tongue.

claims.statement: Images of Pitao Cocijo appear from the Monte Albán II phase, when Zapotec culture was consolidating.
claims.statement_id: Penggambaran Pitao Cocijo muncul sejak Fase Monte Albán II, masa konsolidasi budaya Zapotek.
claims.quote: Las representaciones de Pitao Cocijo aparecen desde la Fase Monte Albán II, en el período de consolidación de la cultura zapoteca

claims.statement: He corresponds to Chaac among the Maya, Tláloc among the Teotihuacanos and Nahuas, and Dzahui among the Mixtecs.
claims.statement_id: Ia padanan Chaac bagi orang Maya, Tláloc bagi orang Teotihuacan dan Nahua, dan Dzahui bagi orang Mixtek.
claims.quote: Es una deidad homóloga a Chaac entre los mayas; Tláloc entre los teotihuacanos y nahuas; y Dzahui entre los mixtecos.

claims.statement: Duppy is a word of African origin used across Caribbean islands, including the Bahamas, Barbados and Jamaica, meaning ghost or spirit.
claims.statement_id: Duppy adalah kata asal Afrika yang dipakai di berbagai pulau Karibia, termasuk Bahama, Barbados, dan Jamaika, dengan arti hantu atau roh.
claims.quote: Duppy is a word of African origin commonly used in various Caribbean Islands, including The Bahamas, Barbados and Jamaica, meaning ghost or spirit.

claims.statement: Duppy are generally seen as malevolent spirits that bring misfortune; they mostly come out to haunt people at night.
claims.statement_id: Duppy umumnya dianggap roh jahat yang membawa kemalangan; mereka terutama keluar dan menghantui orang pada malam hari.
claims.quote: Duppy are generally regarded as malevolent spirits who bring misfortune and woe on those they set upon. They are said to mostly come out and haunt people at night, and people from around the islands claim to have seen them.

claims.statement: The Rolling Calf (a frightening creature bound in chains), the Three footed horse and Ol' Hige are examples of the more malicious spirits.
claims.statement_id: Rolling Calf (makhluk menakutkan berbelit rantai), Three footed horse (kuda berkaki tiga), dan Ol' Hige adalah contoh roh yang lebih jahat.
claims.quote: The "Rolling Calf" (a scary creature said to have chains around its body), "Three footed horse", and "Ol' Hige" are examples of the more malicious spirits.

claims.statement: On many islands of the Lesser Antilles, duppy are called jumbies.
claims.statement_id: Di banyak pulau Antilles Kecil, duppy disebut jumbie.
claims.quote: In many of the islands of the Lesser Antilles, duppy are known as jumbies.

claims.statement: The word duppy comes from the Ga language, as most African folklore in Jamaica comes from the Ashanti people.
claims.statement_id: Kata duppy berasal dari bahasa Ga, karena sebagian besar cerita rakyat Afrika di Jamaika berasal dari orang Ashanti.
claims.quote: The word duppy originates from the Ga language as most of the African folklore and culture in Jamaica comes from the Ashanti people

claims.statement: It may also come from Dapaa, a special Akan day falling 9 days after the first Monday of the month Fwodwo.
claims.statement_id: Kata ini mungkin juga berasal dari Dapaa, hari khusus Akan yang jatuh 9 hari setelah Senin pertama bulan Fwodwo.
claims.quote: It could also originate from the special Akan day Dapaa, which occurs 9 days after the first Monday of the Akan month Fwodwo.

claims.statement: A duppy is an evil ghostly creature of the English-speaking Caribbean tradition.
claims.statement_id: Duppy adalah makhluk hantu jahat dalam tradisi Karibia berbahasa Inggris.
claims.quote: Un duppy est une créature fantomatique maléfique de la tradition anglo-caribéenne.

claims.statement: Another source says the term comes from a Jamaican patois word of uncertain origin meaning "ghost" or "spirit".
claims.statement_id: Sumber lain menyebut istilah ini dari kata patois Jamaika yang asal-usulnya tidak pasti, dengan arti "hantu" atau "roh".
claims.quote: Le terme vient d'un mot de patois jamaïcain d'origine incertaine qui signifie « fantôme » ou « esprit ».

claims.statement: The Greenbrier Ghost is the popular name for the ghost of Elva Zona Heaster Shue, a young woman of Greenbrier County, West Virginia, United States, murdered in 1897.
claims.statement_id: Greenbrier Ghost adalah sebutan populer bagi hantu Elva Zona Heaster Shue, perempuan muda di Greenbrier County, West Virginia, Amerika Serikat, yang dibunuh pada 1897.
claims.quote: The Greenbrier Ghost is the name popularly given to the ghost of Elva Zona Heaster Shue, a young woman in Greenbrier County, West Virginia, United States, who was murdered in 1897.

claims.statement: First ruled a natural death, the court later found she had been murdered by her husband, after her mother Mary Jane Heaster testified that her daughter's spirit revealed the true cause of death.
claims.statement_id: Kematiannya awalnya dianggap wajar, tetapi pengadilan kemudian menyatakan ia dibunuh suaminya, setelah ibunya, Mary Jane Heaster, bersaksi bahwa arwah putrinya mengungkap penyebab kematian sebenarnya.
claims.quote: Initially judged a death by natural causes, the court later declared that the woman had been murdered by her husband, following testimony by the victim's mother, Mary Jane Heaster, in which she claimed that her daughter's spirit revealed the true cause of death.

claims.statement: On 23 January 1897 Zona Shue was found dead at home, and a coroner's jury ruled death by heart disease.
claims.statement_id: Pada 23 Januari 1897 Zona Shue ditemukan tewas di rumahnya, dan juri koroner memutuskan ia meninggal karena penyakit jantung.
claims.quote: On January 23, 1897, Zona Shue was found dead in her home. A coroner's jury rendered a verdict of "death by heart disease".

claims.statement: According to Mary Jane, Zona's spirit insisted Edward had killed her by breaking her neck.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita Mary Jane, arwah Zona bersikeras bahwa Edward membunuhnya dengan mematahkan lehernya.
claims.quote: According to Mary Jane's story, Zona insisted that Edward had killed her by breaking her neck.

claims.statement: Armed with the ghost's story, Mary Jane Heaster went to the local prosecutor, John Alfred Preston.
claims.statement_id: Berbekal cerita dari hantu itu, Mary Jane Heaster mendatangi jaksa setempat, John Alfred Preston.
claims.quote: Armed with the story allegedly told to her by the ghost, Mary Jane Heaster visited the local prosecutor, John Alfred Preston

claims.statement: In October 1896 Zona met Edward Stribbling Trout Shue.
claims.statement_id: Pada Oktober 1896 Zona berkenalan dengan Edward Stribbling Trout Shue.
claims.quote: Im Oktober 1896 machte Zona die Bekanntschaft von Edward Stribbling Trout Shue

claims.statement: In American folklore the hodag is a fearsome critter like a large bull-horned carnivore with a row of thick curved spines down its back.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Amerika, hodag adalah makhluk menakutkan mirip karnivora besar bertanduk banteng dengan deretan duri melengkung di punggungnya.
claims.quote: In American folklore, the hodag is a fearsome critter resembling a large bull-horned carnivore with a row of thick curved spines down its back.

claims.statement: The hodag was said to rise from the ashes of cremated oxen, embodying the abuse they had suffered from their masters.
claims.statement_id: Hodag konon lahir dari abu sapi jantan yang dibakar, sebagai penjelmaan penderitaan hewan-hewan itu di tangan tuannya.
claims.quote: The hodag was said to be born from the ashes of cremated oxen, as the incarnation of the accumulation of abuse the animals had suffered at the hands of their masters.

claims.statement: The hodag's history is tied to Rhinelander, Wisconsin, where it was claimed to be found, and it features in early Paul Bunyan stories.
claims.statement_id: Sejarah hodag erat dengan Rhinelander, Wisconsin, tempat ia diklaim ditemukan, dan ia menonjol dalam kisah awal Paul Bunyan.
claims.quote: The history of the hodag is strongly tied to Rhinelander, Wisconsin, where it was claimed to have been discovered. The hodag has figured prominently in early Paul Bunyan stories.

claims.statement: In 1893 newspapers reported the discovery of a hodag in Rhinelander, Wisconsin.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1893 surat kabar memberitakan penemuan hodag di Rhinelander, Wisconsin.
claims.quote: In 1893, newspapers reported the discovery of a hodag in Rhinelander, Wisconsin.

claims.statement: The reports were started by Eugene Shepard, a well-known Wisconsin land surveyor and prankster who gathered locals to capture the animal.
claims.statement_id: Berita itu digagas Eugene Shepard, juru ukur tanah dan tukang iseng terkenal di Wisconsin, yang mengumpulkan warga untuk menangkap makhluk itu.
claims.quote: The reports were instigated by well-known Wisconsin land surveyor, timber cruiser and prankster Eugene Shepard, who rounded up a group of local people to capture the animal.

claims.statement: According to the tale, it died out after its main food, white bulldogs, became scarce in the area.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita, hodag punah setelah makanan utamanya, anjing bulldog putih, menjadi langka di daerah itu.
claims.quote: It became extinct after its main food source, all white bulldogs, became scarce in the area.

claims.statement: The hodag is an invented animal that is part of the folklore of Wisconsin.
claims.statement_id: Hodag adalah hewan rekaan yang menjadi bagian cerita rakyat negara bagian Wisconsin.
claims.quote: Der Hodag ist ein ausgedachtes Tier, das Teil der Folklore des amerikanischen Bundesstaates Wisconsin ist.

claims.statement: In some legends the ox it rose from belonged to Paul Bunyan, the legendary giant lumberjack.
claims.statement_id: Dalam beberapa legenda, sapi jantan asal hodag adalah milik Paul Bunyan, penebang kayu raksasa legendaris.
claims.quote: in einigen Legenden war es der Ochse von Paul Bunyan, einem sagenumwobenen riesenhaften Holzfäller.

claims.statement: The Horned Serpent appears in the mythologies of many cultures, including Native American, European and Near Eastern.
claims.statement_id: Ular Bertanduk muncul dalam mitologi banyak budaya, termasuk penduduk asli Amerika, Eropa, dan Timur Dekat.
claims.quote: The Horned Serpent appears in the mythologies of many cultures including Native American peoples, European, and Near Eastern mythology.

claims.statement: Details vary, but many stories link it with water, rain, lightning, thunder and rebirth.
claims.statement_id: Rinciannya berbeda antarbudaya, tetapi banyak kisah mengaitkannya dengan air, hujan, petir, guntur, dan kelahiran kembali.
claims.quote: Details vary among cultures, with many of the stories associating the mystical figure with water, rain, lightning, thunder, and rebirth.

claims.statement: Horned Serpents were major elements of the Southeastern Ceremonial Complex of North American prehistory.
claims.statement_id: Ular Bertanduk adalah unsur utama Southeastern Ceremonial Complex dalam prasejarah Amerika Utara.
claims.quote: Horned Serpents were major components of the Southeastern Ceremonial Complex of North American prehistory.

claims.statement: For the Muscogee the Horned Serpent is an underwater serpent with iridescent crystal scales and one large crystal on its forehead, both prized for divination.
claims.statement_id: Bagi orang Muscogee, Ular Bertanduk adalah ular bawah air bersisik kristal berkilau dengan sebuah kristal besar di dahinya; sisik dan kristalnya dihargai karena kekuatan meramal.
claims.quote: To the Muscogee people, the Horned Serpent is a type of underwater serpent covered with iridescent, crystalline scales and a single, large crystal in its forehead. Both the scales and crystals are prized for their powers of divination.

claims.statement: Jackson Lewis, a Muscogee Creek informant to John R. Swanton, said the snake lives in water, has horns like a stag, is not bad and does not harm people, but seems to draw game to it.
claims.statement_id: Jackson Lewis, narasumber Muscogee Creek bagi John R. Swanton, mengatakan ular ini hidup di air, bertanduk seperti rusa, tidak jahat, tidak mencelakai manusia, tetapi seolah punya daya tarik atas hewan buruan.
claims.quote: Jackson Lewis, a Muscogee Creek informant to John R. Swanton, said, "This snake lives in the water has horns like the stag. It is not a bad snake. ... It does not harm human beings but seems to have a magnetic power over game."

claims.statement: In Iroquois tradition the Horned Serpent's anger was thought to raise storms on the lakes.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Iroquois, kemarahan Ular Bertanduk dipercaya menimbulkan badai di danau.
claims.quote: イロコイ諸族（現・イロコイ連邦）の伝承では、ホーンド・ サーペントの怒りが湖に嵐を起こすものと考えられていた。

claims.statement: The Mississauga reportedly never went near a cave by Lake Ontario because a Horned Serpent lived there.
claims.statement_id: Orang Mississauga konon tidak pernah mendekati sebuah gua dekat Danau Ontario karena dihuni Ular Bertanduk.
claims.quote: ミシサグナス族の人々は、オンタリオ湖近くの洞窟にはホーンド・サーペントが棲むために決して近づかなかったという。

claims.statement: Iara is a figure of Brazilian mythology based on Tupi and Guaraní mythology.
claims.statement_id: Iara adalah tokoh mitologi Brasil yang berakar pada mitologi Tupi dan Guaraní.
claims.quote: is a figure from Brazilian mythology based on Tupi and Guaraní mythology.

claims.statement: Iara may have grown from the lore of the carnivorous fish-man Ipupiara, later blended with the European siren or mermaid as the seductress of the Amazon.
claims.statement_id: Iara mungkin berkembang dari kisah Ipupiara, manusia ikan pemakan daging, lalu bercampur dengan mitos siren atau putri duyung Eropa sebagai penggoda Sungai Amazon.
claims.quote: The Iara may have developed from the lore of the carnivorous fish-man Ipupiara ... Conflation with the European myth of the siren, or a beautiful mermaid probably is part of the Iara myth as the seductress of the Amazon River.

claims.statement: Some believe the original Iara was dark-skinned with black hair and eyes like the indigenous people, but in the 19th century she was described as blonde with blue or green eyes, or even green hair.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian penulis meyakini Iara versi asli berkulit gelap, berambut dan bermata hitam seperti penduduk asli, tetapi pada abad ke-19 ia digambarkan pirang dengan mata biru atau hijau, bahkan berambut hijau.
claims.quote: Some commentators believe the original version of Iara must have been dark-skinned and black-haired, black-eyed, like the indigenous populations. However the Iara in the 19th century were described as blonde and blue-eyed or green-eyed, or even green haired.

claims.statement: The word comes from Nheengatu iiyara, from ií "water" + yara "lord; lady".
claims.statement_id: Kata ini berasal dari bahasa Nheengatu iiyara, dari ií "air" dan yara "tuan; nyonya".
claims.quote: The word derives from Nheengatu iiyara, from ií "water" + yara "lord; lady".

claims.statement: Nineteenth-century Romantic poetry later gave her blonde hair, or green hair the colour of vegetation.
claims.statement_id: Puisi para penulis Romantik abad ke-19 kemudian memberinya rambut pirang atau hijau seperti tetumbuhan.
claims.quote: Later, the poetry by Romantic writers in the 19th century would give her blonde hair, or green hair of the color of vegetation.

claims.statement: In Brazilian mythology Iara is a siren.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Brasil, Iara adalah sejenis siren.
claims.quote: ist in der brasilianischen Mythologie eine Sirene.

claims.statement: She has green eyes and lives in rivers or lakes, where at night, especially by moonlight, she sings irresistible songs.
claims.statement_id: Ia bermata hijau dan tinggal di sungai atau danau, tempat ia menyanyikan lagu yang tak tertahankan pada malam hari, terutama saat bulan bersinar.
claims.quote: Sie hat grüne Augen und lebt in den Flüssen oder Seen, wo sie nachts, vor allem bei Mondschein, unwiderstehliche Lieder singt.

claims.statement: Her voice is so beautiful and moving that it enchants men, who follow her to her realm at the bottom of the water.
claims.statement_id: Suaranya begitu indah dan menyentuh sehingga memikat para lelaki, yang lalu mengikutinya ke kerajaannya di dasar air.
claims.quote: Man sagt, sie habe eine so schöne und rührende Stimme, dass sie die Männer damit verzaubert, die ihr in ihr Reich am Grunde des Wassers folgen.

claims.statement: The ghost of U.S. president Abraham Lincoln, also called the White House Ghost, is said to have haunted the White House since his assassination in 1865.
claims.statement_id: Hantu Presiden AS Abraham Lincoln, yang juga disebut Hantu Gedung Putih, konon menghantui Gedung Putih sejak Lincoln dibunuh pada 1865.
claims.quote: The ghost of U.S. president Abraham Lincoln, also known as the White House Ghost, is said to have haunted the White House since Lincoln's assassination in 1865.

claims.statement: His ghost is also said to haunt his former homes in Springfield, Illinois, including his old law office.
claims.statement_id: Hantunya juga dikatakan menghantui bekas kediamannya di Springfield, Illinois, termasuk bekas kantor hukumnya.
claims.quote: Lincoln's ghost has also been said to haunt many of his former residences in Springfield, Illinois, including his former law office.

claims.statement: First Lady Grace Coolidge, Queen Wilhelmina of the Netherlands, Prime Minister Winston Churchill and President Theodore Roosevelt are said to have claimed seeing Lincoln's ghost in the White House.
claims.statement_id: Ibu Negara Grace Coolidge, Ratu Wilhelmina dari Belanda, Perdana Menteri Winston Churchill, dan Presiden Theodore Roosevelt disebut pernah mengaku melihat hantu Lincoln di Gedung Putih.
claims.quote: First Lady Grace Coolidge, Queen Wilhelmina of the Netherlands, Prime Minister Winston Churchill, and President Theodore Roosevelt are among those claimed to have stated they saw Lincoln's ghost in the White House.

claims.statement: The first person reported to see it was Grace Coolidge, who in 1927 saw Lincoln standing at a window of the Yellow Oval Room gazing at the Potomac.
claims.statement_id: Orang pertama yang dilaporkan melihatnya adalah Grace Coolidge, yang pada 1927 melihat Lincoln berdiri di jendela Yellow Oval Room menatap Sungai Potomac.
claims.quote: The first person reported to have actually seen Lincoln's spirit was First Lady Grace Coolidge, who said she saw the ghost of Lincoln standing at a window in the Yellow Oval Room staring out at the Potomac in 1927.

claims.statement: The most famous incident came in 1942: Queen Wilhelmina heard footsteps, answered a knock and saw Lincoln in frock coat and top hat, then fainted.
claims.statement_id: Kejadian paling terkenal terjadi pada 1942: Ratu Wilhelmina mendengar langkah kaki, membuka pintu yang diketuk, dan melihat Lincoln bermantel panjang dan bertopi tinggi, lalu pingsan.
claims.quote: Perhaps the most famous incident was in 1942 when Queen Wilhelmina of the Netherlands allegedly heard footsteps outside her White House bedroom and answered a knock on the door, only to see Lincoln in frock coat and top hat standing in front of her (she promptly fainted).

claims.statement: According to a 1996 Dutch newspaper article, she did not faint but saw the faintly familiar man vanish before she could speak.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel koran Belanda tahun 1996, ia tidak pingsan, melainkan melihat lelaki yang agak dikenalnya itu menghilang sebelum ia sempat berbicara.
claims.quote: According to a Dutch 1996 newspaper article she did not faint, but saw the man, who looked slightly familiar to her, disappear before she could say anything.

claims.statement: In the early 1870s the widowed Mary was photographed at spirit photographer William H. Mumler's studio; behind her appeared a man she said resembled her late husband.
claims.statement_id: Pada awal 1870-an, sang janda Mary berfoto di studio fotografer arwah William H. Mumler; di belakangnya tampak sosok lelaki yang ia akui mirip mendiang suaminya.
claims.quote: メアリー未亡人は1870年代前半に、心霊写真家であるウィリアム・H・マムラーの撮影スタジオを訪れて写真を撮ってもらったが、その背後には彼女が亡き夫に似ていると認める男の姿が映っていた。

claims.statement: Paranormal expert Stephen Wagner attributes the photo to double exposure, though it has circulated widely.
claims.statement_id: Pakar paranormal Stephen Wagner menyebut foto itu hasil pencahayaan ganda, tetapi foto itu tersebar luas.
claims.quote: 超常現象専門家のスティーブン・ワグナーはこの写真は二重露光によるものだとしているが、広く配布されている。

claims.statement: The pishtaco is a folk bogeyman of the Andes, especially Peru and Bolivia, that extracts its victims' fat.
claims.statement_id: Pishtaco adalah sosok momok cerita rakyat di Andes, terutama Peru dan Bolivia, yang mengambil lemak korbannya.
claims.quote: is a folkloric boogeyman figure in the Andes region of South America, particularly in Peru and Bolivia, which extracts the fat of its victims.

claims.statement: It is thought to stem from Spanish conquistadors using the corpse fat of Indigenous Peruvians to treat wounds and illnesses.
claims.statement_id: Sosok ini diyakini berasal dari praktik penakluk Spanyol yang memakai lemak jenazah penduduk asli Peru sebagai obat luka dan penyakit.
claims.quote: It is believed to have originated in Spanish conquistadors' practice of using Indigenous Peruvians' corpse fat as treatment for wounds and illnesses.

claims.statement: In central Peru it is called pishtaco, Quechua for "slaughterer", from pishtay, "behead, cut the throat".
claims.statement_id: Di Peru tengah ia disebut pishtaco, dari bahasa Quechua yang berarti "penjagal", dari pishtay, "memenggal, menggorok leher".
claims.quote: In central Peru it is called pishtaco (in Central and Northern Quechua, meaning "slaughterer", from pishtay, "behead, cut the throat")

claims.statement: In the Bolivian Altiplano it has the Aymara names kharisiri ("slaughterer") or lik'ichiri ("fat-maker").
claims.statement_id: Di Altiplano Bolivia ia disebut dengan nama Aymara kharisiri ("penjagal") atau lik'ichiri ("pembuat lemak").
claims.quote: It is called by the Aymara names kharisiri (var. karisiri "slaughterer") or lik'ichiri ("fat-maker") in the Bolivian Altiplano

claims.statement: He is often pictured as a white or mestizo man armed with a long knife for beheading or dismembering victims.
claims.statement_id: Ia sering digambarkan sebagai lelaki kulit putih atau mestizo bersenjata pisau panjang untuk memenggal atau memotong-motong korbannya.
claims.quote: He is often given a white male racial profile (or mestizo), often said to be armed with a long knife, with which he beheads, disembowels, or dismembers his victims

claims.statement: The pishtaco may also leave no visible wound yet cause death after a few days.
claims.statement_id: Pishtaco juga bisa tidak meninggalkan luka sama sekali, tetapi korban meninggal beberapa hari kemudian.
claims.quote: But the pishtaco may also leave no visible wound on the victim, but cause a fatal condition incurring death after a few days.

claims.statement: In the Andean tradition of the Quechua and Aymara in Peru and Bolivia, it is a monstrous, usually white murderer who sucks the fat from the Indigenous people he kills.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Andes orang Quechua dan Aymara di Peru dan Bolivia, ia pembunuh mengerikan, biasanya kulit putih, yang mengisap lemak penduduk asli yang dibunuhnya.
claims.quote: ist in der andinen Tradition der Quechua und Aymara in Peru und Bolivien ein monströser, meist weißer Mörder, der den ermordeten Indigenen das Fett aussaugt.
